review_notes: I read the whole file, plus the related definitions in FourierSpace, FourierRealification and Parabolic/Basic. I also searched the repository for other uses of gradientOfCovector and l2Vec3Equiv, and searched Mathlib's Fourier, Schwartz and PiLp files. I found no clear missing-bundle problem in the main part of the file. `realPartValue`, `complexifyVectorL2`, `l2Vec3Equiv` and `gradientOfCovector` are already bundled as continuous linear maps or equivalences. `fourier_postcompCLM` is a custom proof, and Mathlib has no direct equivalent. I did not compile anything, and I did not check whether `ContinuousLinearMap.pi` and an evaluation map elaborate with the ℂ-module structure on `L2Vec3 →L[ℝ] ℂ`. That is why the one finding below is weak and offered as a hedged improvement. The duplicated Leray and Stokes wrapper theorems, and the `realPartVectorL2Representative` / `realVectorL2Representative` pair, are design or duplication matters rather than missing bundled structure, so I did not report them.

findings.excerpt:
gradientOfCovectorLinear.mkContinuous 2 (by
    intro D
    exact gradientOfCovectorLinear_norm_bound D)
findings.problem: `gradientOfCovector` is built by hand. A plain linear map is defined coordinatewise, then a separate public theorem (about 20 lines of `nlinarith`) proves the crude bound `‖·‖ ≤ 2‖D‖`, and `mkContinuous 2` bundles the two. The map is just the coordinate-evaluation family D ↦ (D (l2BasisVec i))ᵢ with the `PiLp` structure put back on the result. Bundled continuous maps already express this: each `D ↦ D (l2BasisVec i)` is an evaluation CLM, and they can be assembled into a map to `Fin 3 → ℂ` and then into `PiLp 2` via `(PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv 2 ℂ _).symm`. The norm-bound theorem exists only to make this one definition, and it is used nowhere else in the repository.
findings.proposed_change: Define `gradientOfCovector : (L2Vec3 →L[ℝ] ℂ) →L[ℂ] ComplexVec3` as `(PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv 2 ℂ (fun _ : Fin 3 => ℂ)).symm ∘L ContinuousLinearMap.pi (fun i => <evaluation at l2BasisVec i as a ℂ-linear CLM on L2Vec3 →L[ℝ] ℂ>)`. Alternatively, since the domain is finite-dimensional, obtain continuity from `LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap`, so `gradientOfCovectorLinear_norm_bound` and the `mkContinuous` constant 2 disappear. Keep the apply lemma, which is the one consumer `weakTestGradientSchwartz_fourier` needs (`simp [gradientOfCovector, gradientOfCovectorLinear, ...]`). The current proof of that lemma already reduces to a coordinatewise `PiLp.ext`.
findings.benefit: This removes an ad hoc public norm lemma and its `nlinarith` bookkeeping. The continuity of the gradient extraction then follows from the standard bundled constructors instead of a hand-picked constant. It is also easier to see that the map is just coordinate evaluation.
